comment: The panel letters the big knobs with a Greek alpha for acceleration and a Greek mu for friction, and prints DIST, BOUNCE, DRIVE, SHAKE, HI and LO on the range switch, EXP and LIN on the friction switch, and R-theta and XY on the coordinate switch; the two input jacks are lettered X/R and Y/theta and the outputs X, Y and V. The oversampling control is the small number display at the top right. Two things the manual gets wrong about the wall: it is at ten units, not twelve, and it is a circle in both coordinate systems, with no square case in the code (src/Pilfer.cpp:281 and 316). The control voltage jacks are only read while something is patched into them; an unpatched jack contributes nothing rather than zero volts. src/Pilfer.cpp:198 leaves the return value of filterParams uninitialised when neither a knob has moved nor a jack is connected, so the parameter refresh in that state is left to chance.
